title: Cross-Team Release Train: Launch Calendar & Sync Playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Create an operational playbook and shared launch calendar that coordinates release trains for runtime, console, and API so we can ship coordinated bi-weekly releases with predictable SLAs and rollback paths.

Scope:
- Define release windows (primary and fallback) and timezone-aware cutover times for NA/EU/APAC.
- Establish a cross-team owner rotation, release role definitions (release owner, on-call release engineer, QA lead, docs owner).
- Lock a lightweight gating checklist (smoke tests, infra capacity checks, canary metrics, console dashboard sync).
- Integrate with dedicated capacity booking to reserve GPUs for pre-prod validation and final canary runs.
- Produce a calendar template + automated reminders and a single source of truth calendar (Google shared calendar + README).

Background/context: Over the last three quarters we've had multiple mid-release incidents caused by misaligned cutover times (runtime rollouts that outpaced console feature flags) and inconsistent capacity reservations for dedicated customers. This ticket consolidates prior learnings (incidents INC-2025-17, postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/INC-2025-17) and formalizes a repeatable release train.

Deliverables:
- Release Train Playbook (Confluence): docs + ops runbooks.
- Shared Launch Calendar (Google): templates and per-release event metadata.
- Release checklist (GitHub repo) with CI-driven smoke test gating: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-playbook/pull/142
- Rollback and fallback decision tree with example runbooks for canary failure and capacity shortage.
- Post-release handshake checklist for telemetry/OKR signal collection.

Trade-offs considered:
- Blue/Green for console vs rolling canary for runtime: Chosen: rolling canary for runtime due to stateful KV cache constraints; blue/green kept for major console UI toggles where DB schema or migrations are involved.
- Strict freeze windows vs flexible feature flag gating: Chosen: hybrid — short hard freeze (4 hours) around cutover + mandatory feature-gating for non-critical UI flags. This reduces coordination overhead while preserving safety.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Playbook published to Confluence and linked from product README.
- Shared calendar created with timezone-aware templates and >1 release scheduled for March/April.
- CI smoke test gating has at least 3 automated checks and a documented manual override process.
- Two cross-team dry-run rehearsals completed and retro notes captured.

Notes on rollout mechanics:
- Release cadence: bi-weekly minor releases, quarterly major ship.
- Cutover window: preferred UTC 17:00 (NA late morning / EU early evening) with an APAC-friendly fallback UTC 02:00.
- Autoscaling / Dedicated booking: ops to reserve a 2-hour GPU pool for the final canary run; ticket ENG-5012 tracks reservation automation.

Links and artifacts:
- Draft playbook (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELEASE/Release+Train+Playbook+Draft
- Calendar template: https://calendar.google.com/redwood/release-train-template
- Release checklist (PR): https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-playbook/pull/142
- Incident learnings: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/INC-2025-17
